headline: A Laboratory That Runs Its Own DNA Experiments, With People Left Restocking Supplies
text: Mingyu Wu, Haibo Chen and colleagues at Shanghai Jiao Tong University reported Nov. 4, 2026, in Nature that they have built a laboratory that plans and carries out DNA experiments on its own, leaving people to refill reagents and restock labware. Their system, AutoDNA, directs over 20 types of instruments across more than 11,000 steps to make, copy, transcribe and read genetic material. AutoDNA is built instead for experiments with several objectives at once across many kinds of instruments, and the group describes it as a blueprint toward science offered as a service. In four applications, the group reported that AutoDNA matched the yields experts had reached by hand when building DNA with enzymes, and ran protocols concurrently with a 3.2-fold speed-up.
